info.label: What {title} counts
info.revenue:
Sales after discounts and refunds, before VAT, on the day each order was made.
The dashed line is the dates you compare with, matched day by day.
info.sells:
Revenue by booking or event ticket, after discounts and refunds.
Shop items, add-ons and custom amounts are in Other.
info.tickets:
Revenue by ticket type: the price tier a ticket was sold under, such as Adult or Child, shown as booking · tier. After discounts and refunds.
The top 10 are listed. Everything else, including shop items and add-ons, is in Other. Tickets sold are net of refunds.
info.channels: Each column is one day's sales (one hour's for a single day, one week's for a long period), split by where the order came from: at the counter, online on your own website, or through a marketplace. Every column is the whole of its sales, so a quiet day reads as clearly as a busy one. Hover or focus a column for the amounts. After discounts and refunds.
info.pay:
Money taken, by how the guest paid, on the day it was paid. Failed payments are not counted. This is money in, so it includes VAT and does not take refunds off; it can differ from revenue.
Over time shows each method on its own small chart, all on the same scale.
info.visitors: Guests who were booked to come, by the day and hour of their time slot. Every guest in a booking's party counts. Tickets that need no booking are not counted. The total is the Guests figure at the top.
info.checkins:
Guests checked in, placed on the day and hour of the time slot they booked, because a booking records how many arrived, not when.
"Came" is checked-in guests out of guests who were due: those whose time has started, or who have already arrived. A party of 4 with 3 checked in counts as 3.
info.customers:
Customers with a name on their order, each counted once, on the day of the first order they made in these dates. New means that was their first order here. Returning means they had ordered before these dates.
Sales with no name are not counted.
info.guests: Booked guests whose time slot falls in these dates. Arrived is how many checked in. Didn't come is the guests of bookings marked as no-shows.
info.busy: Guests booked to come, by weekday and hour of their time slot, added up over these dates. It shows this period only, not the comparison.
info.timeslots:
Each row is a booking that sells time slots, such as a show, tour, field or lane. Each column is a start time someone booked. The colour is guests booked, added up over these dates; empty means none.
The tooltip says how full that time was: places taken out of places offered. A field or lane counts as one place per start time. Times nobody booked have no column.
info.lead: How many days before the visit the order was made, for orders that include a booking. The dashed outline is the same bucket in the comparison dates.
info.full: Places sold out of places on offer, for each booking that has a schedule, over these dates. The tick is the same booking in the comparison dates.
info.splitCounters: Sales rung up at each physical counter. Each bar is that counter's share of all counter sales. A sale with no counter recorded shows as Counter, not recorded.
info.splitOnline: Sales made on your online storefront, not through a marketplace. Orders don't record which storefront page was used, so this shows the top 3 bookings sold online.
info.splitMarket: Sales from marketplaces such as Viator or Klook. Commission is what each marketplace took, as saved on the order when it was sold. You keep is sales less commission.

note.guests: Guests booked to come in the period.
note.capacity: Places sold out of places on offer.
note.channels: Revenue by where the sale was made.
note.payments: Money taken, by how the guest paid.
note.series: One row per period. Revenue is after discounts and refunds, before VAT. Guests are placed on the day of their time slot.
note.channelDetail: Each channel's own rows: counters, the top bookings sold online, and marketplaces.

def.revenue: Sales after discounts and refunds, before VAT, on the day each order was made. It is the same figure the Analytics page shows.
def.orders: Orders that were paid and not fully refunded.
def.average: Revenue divided by the number of orders.
def.guests: Guests who were booked to come, counted on the day of their time slot, not the day they bought.
def.capacity: Places sold divided by places on offer, for bookings that have a schedule. Shown as a percentage.
def.refunds: Money given back to guests in the period, VAT included.
def.share: A row's part of the total, as a percentage. Shares add up to 100%.
def.change: How far this period is from the previous one: (this − previous) ÷ previous. Empty when there is nothing earlier to compare with.
def.previous: The comparison you chose on the page: the period before, the same dates a year ago, or your own dates. Only drawn where your records reach back that far.
def.checkedIn: Guests who have arrived, counted on the day and hour of the time slot they booked.
def.customers: Customers with a name on their order, each counted once, on the day of their first order in the period. New means their first order ever at this venue.
def.channels: Counter = sold at a till. Own website = sold online without a marketplace. Marketplaces = sold through partners; commission is what the marketplace kept.
def.vat: VAT charged on each line at the rate it was sold at, after discounts and refunds. The VAT export has the full working paper.
def.series: The first sheet is one row per hour, day or week, depending on how long the period is. Previous-period columns line up by position.

table.taxable: Taxable sales and output VAT, by rate

note.taxable: Sales charged VAT, after discounts and refunds. The VAT column is the output VAT to declare.
note.returnTotal: Everything in the period, and the share that refunds already took back out of it.
note.invoice: One row per invoice and VAT rate. An invoice with two rates has two rows.

kpi.outputVatNote: VAT to declare for the period.

def.outputVat: VAT charged to guests on the period's sales, worked out line by line at the rate each was sold at, after discounts and refunds.
def.taxable: Net sales (before VAT) that were charged VAT at a rate above zero.
def.exempt: Net sales that carried no VAT: the exempt class, or a zero rate.
def.net: The amount VAT was charged on: price less discounts, less the refunded share.
def.refunds: A refund takes the same share of net and VAT back. Refunds are deducted from the day of the original sale, not the day the refund was made.
def.invoice: An order's reference. Only paid and part-refunded orders are included; cancelled and fully refunded ones are not.
def.reconcile: The By day and By invoice totals equal the Summary totals and the VAT figure on the Analytics page.
